articles.fullText:
The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations (UN) Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) in the Armenian capital of Yerevan has entered its final stretch.
The conference has adopted 14 decisions and secured more than $1.8 billion in financial commitments. Yet negotiators remain divided over some of the most contentious issues, including who should bear the cost of protecting nature and how global commitments can be translated into measurable results.
With the conference due to conclude on Friday, the focus has shifted from reaffirming global biodiversity goals to reaching agreement on how to achieve them.
Participants attend the COP 17 to the CBD in Yerevan, Armenia, October 27, 2026. 
Tangible progress
The COP17 marks the first global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted in 2022 with 23 targets to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030.
There are encouraging signs of international cooperation, said Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity, noting that nearly 90% of the convention's parties have established national biodiversity targets, while more than 70% have submitted national reports.
The negotiations have also yielded concrete results. Parties have adopted 14 decisions under the convention, covering areas such as invasive alien species, biosafety, gender equality and education.
Funding announcements have added to the summit's momentum, with new commitments from governments, philanthropic organizations and other partners.
The Executive Council of the China-initiated Kunming Biodiversity Fund has approved nine biodiversity conservation projects worth roughly $4.5 million for developing nations, Dong Baotong, vice minister of China's Ministry of Ecology and Environment, said Monday.
China has contributed 400 million yuan (about $60 million) to the fund, which supports biodiversity conservation in developing countries. Schomaker depicted the initiative as an agile instrument for channeling support to where it is needed.
Elsewhere, nine philanthropic organizations pledged $500 million through 2030 for species recovery, while the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund secured over $60 million in new pledges.
These achievements demonstrate that environmental multilateralism is continuing to deliver, even amid profound geopolitical shifts, said Inger Andersen, executive director of the UN Environment Programme (UNEP).
"Nature is not a luxury we protect when economies can afford it," said Andersen. "Nature is what makes economies possible."
An installation sits outside the venue during the COP 17 to the CBD in Yerevan, Armenia, October 27, 2026. 
Obstacles ahead
Securing new financial commitments is one thing; establishing a sustainable, long-term funding model for biodiversity conservation is another.
Despite the pledges announced in Yerevan, countries remain divided over who should contribute to international biodiversity finance, how much they should pay and how the funds should be allocated.
Other sticking points include reforming subsidies and incentives that harm nature, arrangements for indigenous peoples and local communities, and aligning biodiversity action with climate commitments and other international obligations.
Andersen said ministers are attending the conference's final week to help break the deadlock, particularly on resource mobilization and the global review.
"Financing the destruction of nature with 30 dollars against every dollar spent restoring it is like paying 30 people to tear down your house for every one hired to rebuild it," Schomaker said, framing the way forward around three priorities: accountability, alignment and acceleration.
According to Schomaker, "accountability" means identifying where countries are falling short through national reporting and scientific evidence, while "acceleration" means stepping up efforts to meet the framework's 2030 targets. "Alignment" may prove the hardest part, requiring governments to ensure that public budgets, private investment, economic policies and financial incentives reinforce rather than undermine biodiversity objectives.
The private sector is already pressing for change. More than 130 businesses and financial institutions have called for faster reform of incentives harmful to biodiversity.
Yet, for companies and investors, uncertainty remains over how global biodiversity targets will translate into national regulations, investment requirements and standards for measuring conservation results. Without clearer and more consistent rules, even a growing willingness to invest in nature may struggle to produce results at scale.
Meanwhile, the environmental pressures driving the negotiations are intensifying. UNEP's latest Emissions Gap Report warns that global warming could reach 2.8 degrees Celsius this century under current policies, with potentially severe consequences for ecosystems and biodiversity.
The United Nations' State of Biodiversity Action report, released ahead of COP17, found that fewer than half of the national biodiversity targets assessed by countries were on track.
Against this backdrop, much now hinges on the proposed "Yerevan Pathway," a document that identifies measurable priorities to address gaps in implementing global biodiversity targets over the next two years.
The conference has already shown that multilateral cooperation can deliver decisions and mobilize resources. Whether it can also resolve the harder questions of financing and implementation will be the real test of its success.
"COP17 will be judged by the long-term results we achieve together after the conference, rather than the number of statements made in Yerevan," said Armenian Environment Minister and COP17 President Hambardzum Matevosyan.

paragraphs.en: In 1949, he left China with his family and eventually settled in Missouri. Even after decades away, he {{8}} the dialect he had learned during his childhood in Huangyuan. In 1987, 38 years after leaving China, Plymire returned to Huangyuan. He {{9}} with former neighbors and childhood friends, and revisited the old house where he had once lived. That homecoming marked the beginning of his decades-long {{10}} to supporting local healthcare.
paragraphs.cn: “那时我十几岁。我永远是湟源的男孩。”Plymire于1932年刚满一岁时随父母搬到湟源。他的父亲Victor G. Plymire于1908年首次来到中国，后来定居湟源，在那里建立了一家诊所为当地居民提供医疗服务。成长过程中，Plymire与当地孩子一起玩耍，学会了湟源方言，并熟悉了县里的风俗和生活节奏。

articles.fullText:
Screenshot from a video shows David Victor Plymire, who once described Huangyuan as his one and only hometown at an event. /CMG
David Victor Plymire, 95, was born in New York, the United States. But the place he calls home is Huangyuan, a county in northwest China's Qinghai Province, where he spent 17 years growing up and later devoted decades to improving local healthcare.
In September 2026, during an interview at his home in Missouri, Plymire was looking through a photo album when he came across a photograph of himself as a teenager in Huangyuan, taken in 1942. Pointing himself out in the picture, he spoke in fluent Huangyuan dialect, "That's me. I was in my teens then. I'll always be a boy from Huangyuan."
Plymire moved to Huangyuan with his parents in 1932, shortly after turning one. His father, Victor G. Plymire, first arrived in China in 1908 and later settled in Huangyuan, where he established a clinic to provide medical care to local residents.
Growing up, Plymire played with local children, learned the Huangyuan dialect and became familiar with the customs and rhythms of life in the county. In 1949, he left China with his family and eventually settled in Missouri. Even after decades away, he retained the dialect he had learned during his childhood in Huangyuan.
In 1987, 38 years after leaving China, Plymire returned to Huangyuan. He reunited with former neighbors and childhood friends, and revisited the old house where he had once lived. That homecoming marked the beginning of his decades-long commitment to supporting local healthcare.
Bringing better healthcare to his hometown
During his return visit, Plymire learned that local medical facilities lacked adequate equipment and that many patients had to travel to Xining, Qinghai's provincial capital, for medical examinations.
In March 1989, Plymire and his sister purchased an ultrasound scanner in Hong Kong for 150,000 Hong Kong dollars (about $19,230). With transportation and logistics challenging at the time, he personally accompanied the equipment on its journey to Huangyuan.
The scanner enabled doctors at local medical facilities to conduct basic examinations. Common conditions such as cholecystitis and gallstones could be detected locally, allowing patients to receive initial examinations closer to home and reducing the need for long-distance travel.
A file photo taken in 2000 shows David Victor Plymire and a CT scanner he donated to a hospital in Huangyuan County, northwest China's Qinghai Province. /Xinhua
Since then, Plymire continued to raise funds for medical equipment for local healthcare facilities, helping bring in equipment such as gastroscopes, cardiac monitors and anesthesia machines.
Plymire has helped to raise funds and donate 31 pieces of medical equipment for Huangyuan County People's Hospital, with a combined value of more than 6 million yuan (about $900,000), according to Xinhua News agency.
Over the past three decades, Plymire has traveled between the United States and China more than 20 times. He once spoke about his work for Huangyuan in local dialect, "I regard myself as one of the people of Huangyuan. We Huangyuan folks are one big family, like brothers and sisters. That's why what I've done isn't really a contribution. It's just mutual help among our Huangyuan family."
Preserving a shared history for future generations
Having received his early education in Huangyuan, Plymire understood the challenges facing children in areas where educational resources were relatively limited. He helped connect local schools with foreign teachers and arrange English-language training for primary and secondary school teachers.
Beyond supporting education, Plymire also helped preserve an important part of Huangyuan's history.
His father, Victor G. Plymire, was an accomplished photographer who took hundreds of photographs documenting social life in what are now Gansu Province, Qinghai Province and Xizang Autonomous Region, preserving a valuable visual record of the region's past.
Plymire donated hundreds of his father's photographs to Huangyuan. Drawing on the collection, the county brought together experts and scholars to compile and publish a photo book, helping fill a gap in its historical photographic archives.
David Victor Plymire (second from left) poses for a family photo with his parents and sister. /CMG
Remaining close to the people of Huangyuan
Having grown up in Huangyuan and spent decades giving back to the county, Plymire earned the affection and respect of local residents.
In 2013, Huangyuan held its first "Most Beautiful People of Huangyuan" selection, recognizing individuals who had made outstanding contributions to the community. Plymire was elected as the first international honoree.
Today, at 95, Plymire is no longer able to visit Huangyuan due to his age and health. But he remains in close contact with old friends in the town. Every Mid-Autumn Festival and Spring Festival, he exchanges greetings with them over the phone or by video call.
Though Plymire has lived in the United States for decades, Huangyuan remains the place he calls home. "A person only has one hometown in life, Huangyuan is my only and eternal hometown," he noted.

95岁的David Victor Plymire出生于美国纽约。但他称之为家的地方是中国西北青海省的湟源县，他在那里度过了17年的成长时光，后来数十年致力于改善当地医疗。2026年9月，在密苏里州的家中接受采访时，Plymire正在翻阅一本相册，偶然看到一张1942年拍摄的他在湟源少年时期的照片。他指着照片中的自己，用流利的湟源方言说：“那是我。”

“那时我十几岁。我永远是湟源的男孩。”Plymire于1932年刚满一岁时随父母搬到湟源。他的父亲Victor G. Plymire于1908年首次来到中国，后来定居湟源，在那里建立了一家诊所为当地居民提供医疗服务。成长过程中，Plymire与当地孩子一起玩耍，学会了湟源方言，并熟悉了县里的风俗和生活节奏。

1949年，他与家人离开中国，最终定居密苏里州。即使离开数十年，他仍保留着童年时在湟源学到的方言。1987年，离开中国38年后，Plymire回到湟源。他与旧邻居和儿时朋友重逢，并重访了他曾居住的老房子。那次回乡标志着他数十年支持当地医疗事业的开始。

为故乡带来更好的医疗

在回访期间，Plymire了解到当地医疗设施缺乏足够设备，许多患者不得不前往青海省会西宁进行医学检查。1989年3月，Plymire和妹妹在香港以15万港币（约合19,230美元）购买了一台超声波扫描仪。由于当时运输和物流困难，他亲自陪同设备运往湟源。这台扫描仪使当地医疗机构的医生能够进行基本检查。胆囊炎和胆结石等常见疾病可以在当地检测，使患者能够在离家更近的地方接受初步检查，减少了长途奔波的需要。

2000年拍摄的一张档案照片显示David Victor Plymire和他捐赠给中国西北青海省湟源县一家医院的CT扫描仪。/新华社

此后，Plymire继续为当地医疗设施筹集资金购买医疗设备，帮助引进了胃镜、心脏监护仪和麻醉机等设备。据新华社报道，Plymire已帮助为湟源县人民医院筹集资金并捐赠了31件医疗设备，总价值超过600万元人民币（约合90万美元）。过去三十年间，Plymire往返中美20多次。他曾用当地方言谈及自己为湟源所做的工作：“我把自己当作湟源人之一。”

“我们湟源人是一个大家庭，像兄弟姐妹一样。所以我所做的算不上什么贡献。这只是我们湟源家庭之间的互相帮助。”

为后代保存共同的历史

Plymire在湟源接受了早期教育，他理解教育资源相对有限地区儿童面临的挑战。他帮助当地学校联系外教，并为中小学教师安排英语培训。除了支持教育，Plymire还帮助保存了湟源历史的重要部分。

他的父亲Victor G. Plymire是一位有成就的摄影师，拍摄了数百张照片，记录了现今甘肃、青海和西藏自治区的社会生活，保存了该地区过去的珍贵视觉记录。Plymire向湟源捐赠了数百张父亲的照片。该县利用这些收藏，召集专家学者编纂并出版了一本摄影集，帮助填补了其历史照片档案的空白。David Victor Plymire（左二）与父母和妹妹合影。

/CMG

与湟源人民保持亲近

在湟源长大并数十年回馈该县，Plymire赢得了当地居民的喜爱和尊重。2013年，湟源举办了首届“湟源最美人物”评选，表彰为社区做出突出贡献的个人。Plymire被选为首位国际获奖者。如今，95岁的Plymire因年龄和健康原因无法再访问湟源。但他与镇上的老朋友保持着密切联系。

每逢中秋节和春节，他都会通过电话或视频通话与他们互致问候。尽管Plymire在美国生活了数十年，湟源仍然是他称之为家的地方。他说：“一个人一生只有一个故乡，湟源是我唯一且永恒的故乡。”

articles.title: A Pakistani brand's journey into China's market at CIIE
articles.titleCn: 一个巴基斯坦品牌在进博会进入中国市场的旅程
articles.summary: A Pakistani brand's journey into China's market at CIIE
articles.summaryCn: 本文通过巴基斯坦品牌Hemani Herbals参加中国国际进口博览会的案例，展示了中国通过进博会等制度性安排为全球南方国家出口商提供市场准入机会，并推动中巴经贸合作不断深化。

paragraphs.en: Editor's note: This article was co-authored by Madiha Abid Ali, Anchorperson & Journalist of Pakistan Television News, and Yu Hongyu, a CGTN reporter. The views expressed are the authors' own and do not necessarily reflect those of CGTN. The National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), venue of the 9th China International Import Expo, in Shanghai, China, November 5, 2026. When a company from the Global South steps onto the floor of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), it is stepping into an opportunity China has {{0}} built. The world's first national-level import-themed expo was {{1}} not as a trade show where exhibitors must fight for attention, but as a platform where a rising economic power opens its market and says: come, sell here, grow with us.
paragraphs.cn: 编者按：本文由巴基斯坦电视台新闻主播兼记者Madiha Abid Ali和CGTN记者于洪宇共同撰写。所表达的观点仅代表作者本人，不一定反映CGTN的立场。2026年11月5日，中国上海，第九届中国国际进口博览会举办地——国家会展中心（上海）。当一家来自全球南方的公司踏入中国国际进口博览会（CIIE）的展厅时，它便踏入了一个中国精心构建的机遇。这个世界首个以进口为主题的国家级博览会，其构想并非一个参展商必须争抢关注的贸易展会，而是一个崛起中的经济大国开放其市场并宣告的平台：来吧，在这里销售，与我们共同成长。

paragraphs.en:
For Pakistani brands, that invitation carries the warmth of an {{2}} friendship, one forged through decades of All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership and deepened daily under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor. From first handshake to lasting partnership
The Hemani Herbals booth at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai on November 6, 2026. /Madiha Abid Ali
Hemani Herbals is a {{3}} example of what this partnership looks like in practice. One of Pakistan's largest producers of natural and herbal goods, the company carries over 2,500 health and wellness products and already ships to more than 85 countries. At CIIE, Hemani found what years of independent {{4}} could not: direct access to Chinese importers, distributors, and e-commerce decision-makers under one roof.
paragraphs.cn: 对于巴基斯坦品牌而言，这一邀请承载着铁杆友谊的温暖，这种友谊经过数十年全天候战略合作伙伴关系的锻造，并在中巴经济走廊下日益深化。从首次握手到持久合作。2026年11月6日，在上海举行的第九届中国国际进口博览会（CIIE）上，Hemani Herbals的展位。/Madiha Abid Ali。Hemani Herbals是这种伙伴关系在实践中如何运作的一个有力例证。作为巴基斯坦最大的天然和草本产品生产商之一，该公司拥有超过2500种健康与保健产品，并已出口至85个以上国家。在进博会上，Hemani找到了多年独立拓展未能实现的东西：在一个屋檐下直接接触中国进口商、分销商和电子商务决策者。

paragraphs.en: The expo's design:one-on-one {{5}} matchmaking, dedicated country pavilions with {{6}} booth fees, and {{7}} customs channels,is not accidental. It is China's {{8}} answer to the question every Global South exporter faces: how do I go from unknown to stocked? The real prize is not a single expo order. It is the distributor who keeps calling afterward, the storefront that opens on a Chinese e-commerce platform, and the supply agreement that renews because the product earned its shelf. China's 1.4 billion consumers reward brands that invest in local packaging, meet regulatory standards, and price thoughtfully, and that reward is exactly what makes the market worth the effort.
paragraphs.cn: 博览会的设计——一对一采购对接、提供展位费补贴的专门国家馆以及快速通关渠道——并非偶然。这是中国对每个全球南方出口商都面临的问题的制度性回答：我如何从无名之辈变成上架商品？真正的奖赏不是单次博览会的订单，而是之后持续来电的分销商、在中国电商平台上开设的店铺，以及因产品赢得货架而续签的供应协议。中国的14亿消费者会奖励那些在本地包装、符合监管标准和定价 thoughtfully 方面进行投资的品牌，而这种奖励正是使这个市场值得付出努力的原因。

paragraphs.en:
For a company like Hemani, the Chinese consumer is not a gatekeeper to be feared but a partner to be understood. Numbers that tell a story of acceleration
The {{9}} is {{10}}. Pakistan's exports to China reached $2.386 billion in the first eight months of 2026, a 40.51% year-on-year {{11}}, according to China General Administration of Customs data. Refined metals, agriculture, and textiles led the charge, but the range is {{12}} fast: leather goods, handicrafts, fashion, precious stones, and health products are finding Chinese buyers for the first time, both through the Pakistan Pavilion and independent listings. This growth did not happen in a vacuum.
paragraphs.cn: 对于像Hemani这样的公司来说，中国消费者不是令人畏惧的守门人，而是需要理解的合作伙伴。数字讲述了一个加速的故事。势头显而易见。根据中国海关总署的数据，2026年前八个月，巴基斯坦对华出口达到23.86亿美元，同比增长40.51%。精炼金属、农业和纺织品引领增长，但范围正在迅速扩大：皮革制品、手工艺品、时尚产品、宝石和保健品首次通过巴基斯坦馆和独立 listings 找到中国买家。这种增长并非凭空发生。

paragraphs.en: It reflects the second-phase {{13}} of the China-Pakistan Free Trade Agreement, which are set to further reduce {{14}} and expand market access into value-added categories. It reflects China's zero-tariff treatment for least-developed countries, extended and deepened. And it reflects a deliberate policy choice: China is not merely a market that happens to be open, it is actively widening the door for partners who share its vision of mutual development. With room to grow, the task now is to widen the product base so that this momentum becomes a {{15}} current rather than a single wave. CIIE, with its buyer-facing architecture, is precisely the {{16}} that can turn spikes into {{17}} revenue.
paragraphs.cn: 它反映了中巴自由贸易协定第二阶段的谈判，该谈判将进一步降低关税并扩大对增值类别的市场准入。它反映了中国对最不发达国家的零关税待遇得到延长和深化。它还反映了一个深思熟虑的政策选择：中国不仅仅是一个恰好开放的市场，它正在积极为那些与其共同发展愿景一致的伙伴拓宽大门。随着增长空间的存在，现在的任务是扩大产品基础，使这一势头成为持久的潮流而非单一浪潮。进博会以其面向买家的架构，正是能够将峰值转化为经常性收入的加速器。

paragraphs.en:
The road ahead, walked together
Sellers engage directly with Chinese consumers through a livestream at the Pakistan pavilion of the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai on November 6 2026. /Madiha Abid Ali
Pakistani participation at CIIE has grown steadily since the {{18}} edition in 2018. More firms are joining the Pakistan Pavilion each year; more are registering independently, drawn by word-of-mouth success stories. Chinese e-commerce platforms, meanwhile, have launched dedicated programs to help South Asian brands {{19}} cross-border logistics, localization, and consumer engagement, lowering the learning curve that once made China seem {{20}} to first-time exporters. For Hemani, the next chapter is clear: deepening its China strategy, investing in brand-building tailored to Chinese shoppers, and building supply-chain {{21}} that can scale with demand.
paragraphs.cn: 前方的路，携手同行。2026年11月6日，在上海举行的第九届中国国际进口博览会的巴基斯坦馆，卖家通过直播直接与中国消费者互动。/Madiha Abid Ali。自2018年首届以来，巴基斯坦在进博会的参与稳步增长。每年有更多公司加入巴基斯坦馆；更多公司因口碑成功故事而独立注册。与此同时，中国电子商务平台推出了专门项目，帮助南亚品牌应对跨境物流、本地化和消费者互动，降低了曾经让中国对首次出口商显得令人生畏的学习曲线。对于Hemani来说，下一章很明确：深化其中国战略，投资于为中国购物者量身定制的品牌建设，并建立能够随需求扩展的供应链韧性。

paragraphs.en: The company that walks into CIIE as a promising newcomer walks out, year after year, as a brand that Chinese families recognize, trust, and reorder. This is what shared growth looks like in practice,not a slogan, but a shelf in a Chinese home carrying a Pakistani-made product, renewed because it earned its place. The National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), venue of the 9th China International Import Expo, in Shanghai, China, November 5, 2026. 
When a company from the Global South steps onto the floor of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), it is stepping into an opportunity China has deliberately built. The world's first national-level import-themed expo was conceived not as a trade show where exhibitors must fight for attention, but as a platform where a rising economic power opens its market and says: come, sell here, grow with us. For Pakistani brands, that invitation carries the warmth of an ironclad friendship, one forged through decades of All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership and deepened daily under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.
From first handshake to lasting partnership
The Hemani Herbals booth at the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai on November 6, 2026. /Madiha Abid Ali
Hemani Herbals is a compelling example of what this partnership looks like in practice. One of Pakistan's largest producers of natural and herbal goods, the company carries over 2,500 health and wellness products and already ships to more than 85 countries. At CIIE, Hemani found what years of independent outreach could not: direct access to Chinese importers, distributors, and e-commerce decision-makers under one roof. The expo's design:one-on-one procurement matchmaking, dedicated country pavilions with subsidized booth fees, and expedited customs channels,is not accidental. It is China's institutional answer to the question every Global South exporter faces: how do I go from unknown to stocked?
The real prize is not a single expo order. It is the distributor who keeps calling afterward, the storefront that opens on a Chinese e-commerce platform, and the supply agreement that renews because the product earned its shelf. China's 1.4 billion consumers reward brands that invest in local packaging, meet regulatory standards, and price thoughtfully, and that reward is exactly what makes the market worth the effort. For a company like Hemani, the Chinese consumer is not a gatekeeper to be feared but a partner to be understood.
Numbers that tell a story of acceleration
The momentum is unmistakable. Pakistan's exports to China reached $2.386 billion in the first eight months of 2026, a 40.51% year-on-year surge, according to China General Administration of Customs data. Refined metals, agriculture, and textiles led the charge, but the range is broadening fast: leather goods, handicrafts, fashion, precious stones, and health products are finding Chinese buyers for the first time, both through the Pakistan Pavilion and independent listings.
This growth did not happen in a vacuum. It reflects the second-phase negotiations of the China-Pakistan Free Trade Agreement, which are set to further reduce tariffs and expand market access into value-added categories. It reflects China's zero-tariff treatment for least-developed countries, extended and deepened. And it reflects a deliberate policy choice: China is not merely a market that happens to be open, it is actively widening the door for partners who share its vision of mutual development.
With room to grow, the task now is to widen the product base so that this momentum becomes a durable current rather than a single wave. CIIE, with its buyer-facing architecture, is precisely the accelerant that can turn spikes into recurring revenue.
The road ahead, walked together
Sellers engage directly with Chinese consumers through a livestream at the Pakistan pavilion of the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai on November 6 2026. /Madiha Abid Ali
Pakistani participation at CIIE has grown steadily since the inaugural edition in 2018. More firms are joining the Pakistan Pavilion each year; more are registering independently, drawn by word-of-mouth success stories. Chinese e-commerce platforms, meanwhile, have launched dedicated programs to help South Asian brands navigate cross-border logistics, localization, and consumer engagement, lowering the learning curve that once made China seem forbidding to first-time exporters.
For Hemani, the next chapter is clear: deepening its China strategy, investing in brand-building tailored to Chinese shoppers, and building supply-chain resilience that can scale with demand. The company that walks into CIIE as a promising newcomer walks out, year after year, as a brand that Chinese families recognize, trust, and reorder.
This is what shared growth looks like in practice,not a slogan, but a shelf in a Chinese home carrying a Pakistani-made product, renewed because it earned its place. China's opening-up is not a one-time gesture; it is a commitment renewed with each expo, each policy round, each partnership deepened. And for the Global South, the message is simple: the door is open, the path is clear, and the growth is meant to be shared.

A document confirming the transfer of the US airmen remains found along Hump Route is signed, witnessed by Chinese and American representatives, during a handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, November 10, 2026. /Xinhua
Chinese honor guards walked forward, carrying a box containing human remains. US honor guards stepped up to receive it and carefully placed an American national flag over the box.
The box held eight bone fragments recovered from a glacier more than 5,000 meters above sea level. The remains, believed to belong to US airmen who went missing along the Hump Route during World War II (WWII), had lain in the mountains for more than 80 years.
At the handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, on Tuesday, He Jiang, director of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Archives, and US Navy Captain Colin Alexander Eliot, a forensic expert with the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA), signed a document confirming the transfer, witnessed by Chinese and American representatives.
Chinese honor guards handover the box containing the US airmen remains found along Hump Route during a handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, November 10, 2026. /Xinhua
The remains were recovered in areas along the Hump Route, which was established after Japanese forces occupied Myanmar in 1942, cutting off the Yunnan-Myanmar road, China's last major overland supply link to the outside world.
Stretching from the state of Assam in northeastern India to Kunming in southwest China, the air corridor across the Himalayas became a vital lifeline for Allied supplies supporting China's resistance against Japanese aggression from 1942 to 1945.
The route crossed snow-covered mountains, deep gorges, glaciers and tropical forests. Violent air currents, low air pressure, hail and freezing conditions posed constant risks to aircraft flying through the region. It became known as the "death route."
More than 1,000 Chinese and American aircrew members lost their lives along the route. With the high mountains and glaciers making searches exceptionally difficult, many of their remains have never been recovered.
The fragments handed over on Tuesday were found by a search team organized by Jianchuan Museum, a privately-run museum in Sichuan, during expeditions to the glaciers of Nyingchi in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region.
The searchers trekked through primeval forests and waded across rushing rivers, taking care to avoid bears in the mountains and deadly hazards on the glaciers. After repeated searches, they finally located the remains.
China and the United States have cooperated in searching for American military personnel missing during WWII since the 1970s. Both Chinese authorities and civilian groups have contributed to those efforts.
An official with the general office of the Central Military Commission, who attended the ceremony, said the joint efforts to recover the remains of missing US servicemen were a testament to the two countries' history of fighting side by side against Japanese fascism during WWII.
China has long supported the search on humanitarian grounds and is willing to continue practical cooperation with the United States in this field, the official said, adding that such efforts could contribute positively to building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability.
"These remains bear witness to the war against fascism and carry the history of the Chinese and American peoples fighting aggression together," said Fan Jianchuan, curator of Jianchuan Museum. "They also remind us to strengthen cooperation and make new contributions to world peace."
US honor guards receive the box containing the US airmen remains found along Hump Route during a handover ceremony in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, November 10, 2026. /Xinhua
Addressing the ceremony, Eliot spoke of the shared wartime history that the remains represent.
"The remains before us represent a defining historical moment when Americans, compelled by duty to defend against aggression, stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the people of China to fight that very same threat," he said.
Following the ceremony, Chinese and US representatives visited the Hall of the Heroes of the Flying Tigers, which commemorates the Flying Tigers and other American servicemen who assisted China during WWII.
Through wartime artifacts and other displays, the exhibition documents the history of Chinese and American cooperation against Japanese aggression. It has received more than 10 million visitors since opening over two decades ago.
The airmen's identities have yet to be established. After the remains reach the United States, the DPAA will conduct DNA testing, examine historical evidence, and compare military records. Families will be notified only after identification is confirmed.
